title: What Is Software? (Rules vs Learning)
status_note: Draft script by Claude. Not fact-checked. General concept, no product claims.
learning_objective: Viewer understands software as step-by-step instructions written by humans, which sets up the contrast with AI.
analogy: A recipe card (software) vs a chef who has cooked thousands of meals (learning from experience).
analogy_breaks: A chef tastes and understands the food. A learning system only finds patterns in examples; it doesn't taste or understand.
actual_tech: Traditional software executes explicit instructions written by programmers; deterministic for the same input.
fact_check_notes: General concept. Some software contains randomness; episode says 'usually same input, same output'.
takeaway: Software is instructions a computer follows.
cta: One tech concept. One simple story.

phrases.text: Hey techies! Sneha here from Zillenial Talk.
phrases.say: Hey techies! Sneha here from Zillennial Talk.

phrases.text: Before we talk AI, we need one word: software.
phrases.say: Before we talk A.I., we need one word: software.

phrases.text: Think of software as a recipe card.
A human writes every step, and the computer follows them exactly.
So, usually, the same ingredients give the same dish, every time.
AI is different. It's more like a chef who's cooked thousands of meals.
phrases.say: A.I. is different. It's more like a chef who's cooked thousands of meals.

phrases.text: Nobody handed that chef a card for every dish.
Quick reality check: a chef can taste the soup.
An AI model only finds patterns in examples. It doesn't taste or understand.
phrases.say: An A.I. model only finds patterns in examples. It doesn't taste or understand.

phrases.text: So software is instructions a computer follows.
Next up: what AI actually is.
phrases.say: Next up: what A.I. actually is.

phrases.text: One tech concept. One simple story. I'm Sneha, and this is Zillenial Talk.
phrases.say: One tech concept. One simple story. I'm Sneha, and this is Zillennial Talk.
